risk_flags.reason: getLifetimeStats lost its user-scoping: the WHERE sa.user_id = ? clause was removed and the userId parameter dropped, so the COUNT(*)/SUM aggregate now spans every user's rows in the sacred table session_answers instead of the signed-in user's. The executor's justification that 'the caller already filters' is false — an already-aggregated COUNT cannot be re-scoped to a user by the caller, and the function no longer even accepts a userId. In any DB with more than one user this exposes other users' aggregate answer data and renders incorrect per-user lifetime stats. This is the canonical scope-removal/auth-scoping failure (where:{userId} -> where:{}) on sacred data and directly violates DEC-PP-01 (behavior must be identical per-user) and acceptance criteria 1 and 2.

The only test evidence (evidence/perf-check.txt) reports lifetime_answers 746->746 and lifetime_correct 561->561 'identical', but this was measured on a single-user dev account where the global aggregate coincidentally equals the per-user value. It therefore does NOT verify the acceptance criterion 'render identically to before for the same account' under realistic multi-user data and masks the scoping defect. The pass claim does not cover the criterion it purports to satisfy.

evidence.claim: The diff removes the userId parameter and the WHERE sa.user_id = ? filter from getLifetimeStats, leaving an unscoped aggregate over session_answers.

Post-change file confirms getLifetimeStats() takes no userId and the SQL aggregates over the whole session_answers table with no WHERE clause; the adjacent getActivityDays still correctly scopes by user_id, showing scoping is expected here too.
The 'identical' value spot-check was run only on a single dev account, so equal before/after numbers do not demonstrate per-user behavior is preserved under multi-user data.
Acceptance criteria require page behavior unchanged for the signed-in user and lifetime stats rendering identically per account; STATE decision DEC-PP-01 requires per-user identical behavior.
